perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s perspective, she has access to the following:

- Sara is a Speech-Language Pathologist and knows Shirley Whiteplume as a long-time nurse colleague and close friend at their community health center.
- A mutual patient died. Sara attended his funeral and saw Shirley there appearing somber. Sara suspected Shirley was deeply affected.
- At the funeral, Sara told Shirley she knew it must be hard and that she had seen how much Shirley cared for him. Sara heard Shirley say it had been tough and that she kept thinking whether more could have been done. Sara replied that they did everything they could and should remember the good care and moments of joy they provided. Shirley said Sara was right but it was hard to let go.
- During a work coffee break, Sara raised the patient’s treatment decisions because she sensed Shirley felt burdened. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that Shirley should not carry the burden alone. Shirley said she appreciated that but it was hard to accept.
- After observing Shirley remain reserved and minimally expressive, Sara confronted her in their office. Sara said it was okay to be open about feelings. Shirley said she did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotions does not make someone weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Sara later felt her confrontation might have been too harsh and apologized if she came on too strong. Shirley said it was a bit much but she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara thanked her and said she was there however needed. Shirley thanked her and said continuing to talk helps.
- Later, Sara noticed Shirley seemed improved, felt hopeful, and asked how she was feeling. Shirley said she felt better because of their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggested spending more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and said they could plan something for the weekend.
